newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Decree on Russia's Gazprom ready soon - agency.
newsitem.headline: Decree on Russia's Gazprom ready soon - agency.

text.p: A presidential decree strengthening state control over natural gas producer Gazprom will be drafted in the near future, Interfax news agency said on Monday.

Interfax quoted First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov's press secretary Andrei Pershin as saying that Nemtsov and RAO Gazprom chairman Rem Vyakhirev discussed changes to the agreement by which Vyakhirev manages 35 percent of the government's 40 percent stake at a meeting on Monday.
Interfax said the parties agreed to consolidate Vyakhirev's personal control over the share stake, while clearly outlining his rights and responsibilities under a new trust agreement.
They also agreed to pay off the 15 trillion roubles Gazprom currently owes the government in May and June. The money will be used to pay off government pension and wages arrears.
Reducing the government's debt to Gazprom was also discussed at the meeting.
Nemtsov is leading a government campaign to revamp Russia's natural monopolies, industries which have no competitors, such as gas and electricity, telecommunications and railways.

President Boris Yeltsin boosted the cause, now over a month old, last week when he signed a decree calling on the government to prepare a programme for restructuring, privatising and strengthening state control of the natural monopolies.
